Contracts & Providers

User manual

How to ask for a purchase, keep your contracts and their renewals, and decide what is sent to you. For everyone who uses Six7 Contracts & Providers, and for the approvers and Procurement Managers.

1. Getting started#

1.1 What Contracts & Providers is for#

Contracts & Providers is where your company keeps its contracts, its providers (the companies it buys from) and its purchase requests. You use it to:

  • ask for a purchase, a one-off item or a service paid over months or years, and follow it until it arrives;
  • keep your contracts: their dates, value, exit terms and files, so that no renewal or notice deadline takes anyone by surprise;
  • decide, if you're an approver, on the purchases and renewals your company's rules send you.

Each morning, Home shows what needs you.

Why Six7, and how its apps work, is in the Suite manual.

1.2 Opening the app#

Open the link you were given and bookmark it. Google signs you in with your work account: there's no separate password. See Suite §5 if you use several Google accounts.

If the app says "Sign in with your work account" or "You don't have access to Six7 Contracts & Providers yet", see Suite §5.

1.3 Your role#

Your role is shown at the top right, under your name:

  • Individual: you see your own contracts and their obligations, the obligations you own, your purchase requests, the items sent to you for a decision, and the provider directory.
  • Procurement Manager: you see everything, providers' documents included, and look after the data.
  • Admin: you see everything and run the app.

Approvers can have any role. You're one if you're in Group 1 (the standard approvers) or Group 2 (the senior approvers). What waits for your decision is in Approvals.

Each task below says who can do it. The general model is in Suite §6.

2. A tour of the app#

The bar at the top has Home, Approvals (with the number of items waiting for you), Contracts, Providers, Obligations, Purchases and Reports. Procurement Managers and Admins also see Admin tools. On the right: the search box, a refresh button, and your initials, which open Your settings.

2.1 Home#

Needs attention: what needs you in the coming weeks, in counts and their lists:

  • Approvals waiting for me: purchases and renewals for you to decide;
  • Renewals coming up: your active contracts ending in the next 90 days, with their renewal review, such as Renews automatically, Review pending, Not renewing or Review opens 1 Dec;
  • Notice deadlines: your contracts whose notice deadline is in the next 30 days, or has passed while the contract still runs;
  • Provider documents (Procurement Managers and Admins): expired or expiring;
  • Obligations due: yours, overdue or due in the next 7 days, each with Mark done.

Click a count to go to its list, and a row to open it. Overdue and urgent items are in red. At the top: New contract and New purchase request.

Procurement Managers and Admins switch Home between Mine and All (the default). Approvals waiting for you are always your own. When nothing needs you, Home says "All clear — nothing needs attention in the next 90 days."

2.2 Approvals#

Waiting for me lists everything waiting for your decision, purchases and renewals together. Each item shows its value, term and exit terms, the group and rule that sent it to you, and who asked or owns the contract. Decided by me shows your decisions of the last 90 days.

Click an item to open its decision panel: the facts the rule used, the rule's description, and the buttons to decide (§3.3, §3.4).

2.3 Contracts#

The Contracts list shows active, draft and under-review contracts by default, with their status, end date, notice deadline and renewal value. Badges flag what needs attention: Expiring, Notice due, Review pending, Renews automatically, Renewal approved and Not renewing. Filter by Status, Type, Ending within and Review; Procurement Managers also by Owner and Archived.

Click a contract to open its panel:

  • Terms: type, fee, dates, renewal, notice period and deadline, what ending it early costs, and the renewal value;
  • Renewal review: when it opens, or its outcome, rule, approvers and decision, and Record notice sent when it's needed;
  • Obligations, with Add obligation;
  • Files and history: the contract document, the signed copy, and the renewal chain (Renewed from, Renewed as);
  • Edit, Renew, History, Copy link and Archive.

2.4 Providers#

The provider directory: every provider with its status, compliance (OK, Expiring, Expired or No documents), owner and active contracts. Filter by Status, Category and Compliance.

A provider's panel shows its contact details, its Documents, and the contracts and purchase requests with it that you can see. Only Procurement Managers and Admins see the documents; everyone else sees the provider's compliance.

2.5 Obligations#

What contracts commit you to do: payments, deliverables, reviews. The list shows the Open ones by default (or Done, or All), with the due date, contract, owner and recurrence. Tick Done when one is done. Filter by Due within; Procurement Managers also by Owner.

2.6 Purchases#

Your purchase requests, with their type, total contract value, status and needed-by date. Procurement Managers and Admins also have All. Filter by Status and Type.

A request's panel shows its status steps with their dates, the total contract value and its breakdown, where the rules sent it, the justification and the decision, and the buttons you can use now.

2.7 Reports#

Six reports about contracts, spend, approvals, compliance and obligations: chapter 6.

3. Everyday tasks#

3.1 Ask for a purchase#

  1. Click New purchase request, on Home or Purchases.
  2. Choose Single purchase, or Recurring fees (months or years) for a service you pay every month, quarter or year.
  3. Type a Title. Choose the Provider, or Not registered yet and type its name. Check the Currency.
  4. For a single purchase, enter the Price. For recurring fees:
    • the Setup or one-time fee, if there is one;
    • the Recurring fee, and how it's Billed: monthly, quarterly or annually;
    • the Committed term, in months (12, 24 and 36 are one click);
    • If we end it early: no cost, an early-termination fee (and its amount), or the rest of the term.
  5. Add Needed by, the Related contract if there is one, and the Justification: approvers read it first.
  6. Look at the box on the right: the Total contract value, and where the request will go, for example "Will go to Group 1 (rule P3), standard approvers".
  7. Click Submit for approval, or Save draft to finish it later.

  • The total contract value of recurring fees is the setup fee plus every payment of the term: 150 a month for 36 months is 5,400. A term that doesn't fill its last period counts it whole: 13 months billed quarterly is 5 payments.
  • If the request is approved automatically by your company's rules, the button reads Submit (approved automatically), and it's approved as soon as you submit it.
  • A draft can be incomplete. Submit checks every field.
  • If the provider is Suspended or Inactive, the form says so.

3.2 Follow your request#

Open it from Purchases, or search for it. Its status steps show where it is, and when each step happened.

  • Submitted: waiting for an approver. You can still Cancel request.
  • Approved: you get an email. Order it, then click Mark ordered, with the order reference if there is one.
  • Received: click Mark received with the date, and upload the receipt or delivery note, or paste a link. You can do this straight after Approved.
  • Closed: click Close when it's all done.
  • Rejected: you get the approver's comment. Edit the request and Submit for approval again; the rules run again.

Fields can be changed only while the request is a Draft or Rejected. For approved recurring fees, Create contract opens a new contract filled in from the request (§3.5).

Procurement Managers and Admins can take these steps on anyone's request, except editing a rejected one.

3.3 Decide on a purchase#

If you're an approver, you get an email, "Approval needed:" with the title and value, and the request waits in Approvals:

  1. Open it. Read the total contract value and its breakdown, the term, what ending it early costs, the provider's compliance, why it came to you ("Routed to Group 1 by rule P3", with the rule's description) and the justification.
  2. Write a comment: it's required.
  3. Click Approve or Reject. The requester gets an email with your decision and your comment.

Any one approver of the group may decide; once someone has, it leaves the others' lists. You're never asked to decide on your own request. For a request in another currency, the panel says the amounts were compared with the rules without conversion.

3.4 Decide on a renewal#

Some months before a contract ends, your company's rules decide whether its renewal needs a decision. If it does, its approvers get "Renewal decision needed:" with the contract and the date to decide by, and it waits in Approvals:

  1. Open it. Read the renewal value (the fee for one renewal term), the renewal term, what ending it early costs, the notice deadline, whether it renews automatically, the provider's compliance and the rule.
  2. Write a comment: why renew, or why not.
  3. Click Approve renewal or Not renewing. After Not renewing, the contract's owner is emailed to send notice; after you approve a contract that doesn't renew by itself, to use Renew. An approved auto-renewing contract needs nothing more: it rolls over at its end date.

You can decide from the contract's Renewal review box too. In the last 7 days before the deadline the review is Urgent, and the owner, the Procurement Managers and the Admins hear about it in their digest. If nobody decides before the end date, the review lapses: an auto-renewing contract then renews without a decision. You're never asked to decide on a contract you own.

3.5 Register a contract#

  1. Click New contract, on Home or Contracts.
  2. Type the Title. Choose the Type, and the Status: Draft while it's being agreed, Active once it's signed and running.
  3. Choose the Provider: the Counterparty fills in. For a customer, landlord or partner who isn't a provider, leave the provider blank and type the counterparty.
  4. Enter the Value per billing period (for One-off, the total), the Currency and the Billing frequency.
  5. Enter the Start date and the End date. A blank end date means open-ended: no renewal reminders or reviews.
  6. Tick Renews automatically if it does, with the Renewal term (months). Enter the Notice period (days).
  7. Choose If we end it early: None, an early-termination fee (with its amount), or the remaining term payable.
  8. Upload the Contract document and the Signed copy, or paste their links. Click Save.

As you type, the box under the form shows the notice deadline (the end date minus the notice period) and the renewal TCV (the value of one renewal term).

The contract is yours: you see it and get its reminders. Only Active contracts get renewal reviews and renew or end at their end date, so change the status once it's signed. A Procurement Manager can make someone else the owner.

Create contract, on an approved request for recurring fees, opens the same form filled in from the request, linked to it.

3.6 Renew a contract#

For a contract that doesn't renew by itself, or to start a new term with new terms:

  1. Open the contract and click Renew. It's there on Active and Expired contracts, for their owner, Procurement Managers and Admins.
  2. A new contract opens with the details carried over, the dates moved on (it starts the day after the old one ends) and the status Draft. Change what's new.
  3. Click Save renewal. The new contract shows Renewed from, and the old one becomes Renewed.

If the old contract's renewal review is still pending, or was decided as not renewing, Renew asks you to confirm first. Cancel changes nothing.

3.7 When a contract isn't renewing#

When an approver decides Not renewing, the contract's owner gets an email: "Not renewing", the contract, and the date to send notice by.

  1. Send the notice to the counterparty, as the contract requires, before that date.
  2. Open the contract. In its Renewal review box, click Record notice sent: enter the date, and upload the notice letter or paste a link if you want.
  3. The contract no longer renews automatically, and becomes Terminated at its end date.

If nobody records the notice, an auto-renewing contract renews at its end date anyway, and the digest says "Renewed: notice not recorded". The owner, Procurement Managers and Admins can record the notice.

When an approver approves the renewal of a contract that doesn't renew by itself, the owner gets "Renewal approved": they use Renew (§3.6).

3.8 Add a provider and its documents#

  1. On Providers, click New provider.
  2. Type the Name, and add the category, status (Onboarding at first), contact, email, phone, website, tax ID and country.
  3. Click Save. If a provider with the same name or tax ID already exists, the app says which one: click Save anyway if yours is a different provider.

The provider is yours: you and Procurement Managers can edit it.

Documents are added by Procurement Managers and Admins: on the provider's panel, Add document, with its type, title, issue and expiry dates (no expiry date: it doesn't expire), the file and notes. A document is Valid, Expiring (within 30 days) or Expired, and the provider's compliance follows its documents: Expired if any is expired, else Expiring if any is expiring, else OK; No documents without any.

3.9 Track obligations#

  • On a contract, click Add obligation; or New obligation on Obligations, and choose the contract.
  • Enter a Description and a Due date, and choose the Owner (by default the contract's owner) and the Recurrence: None, Monthly, Quarterly or Annual.
  • Tick Done, or click Mark done on Home, when it's done. A recurring obligation then creates the next one, one period later. Unticking it doesn't remove the next one.

An obligation can be changed by its owner, the contract's owner, Procurement Managers and Admins.

3.10 Files#

For a contract, a signed copy, a provider document, a receipt or a notice letter, click Upload a file (up to 10 MB), or paste a link.

  • Uploaded files go to the app's own Drive folder. Each opens only for the people who may see its record, and nobody gets a "shared with you" email.
  • A link to a file in that folder works only for a file you can already open. To attach someone else's file, upload a copy.

3.11 Archive and restore#

Nothing is deleted.

  • Archive: a contract's or a provider's owner, or a Procurement Manager, clicks Archive on its panel. Obligations are archived from their form, by whoever may change them. It leaves the lists, Home and search. Archiving a contract takes it, its obligations and its renewal off Home and the digest. Settle a pending renewal review before you archive its contract: archiving doesn't close the review, and it stays in its approvers' Approvals.
  • Purchase requests aren't archived: cancel one instead, while it's a Draft or Submitted.
  • Restore: Procurement Managers and Admins tick Archived on Contracts or Providers, open the record and click Restore.

4. Working with others#

How a purchase request and a renewal move through the app, and who acts at each step. Your company may work differently today: compare it with these pages before the app goes live. The Configuration manual's §1.5 says what your Admin can change and what this release fixes.

4.1 A purchase request's journey#

From asking to closing, the app routes the request and tells people by itself; people ask, decide and confirm.

4.2 Purchase request statuses#

A request is always in one of eight statuses. §3.2 says what each action does.

4.3 Who decides#

Your company's rules decide where each request and each renewal goes. They're checked from the top, and the first one that matches decides. Each item shows the rule that sent it, for example "Routed to Group 1 by rule P3", with the rule's description.

With the rules the app starts with:

A purchaseGoes to
A single purchase under 50, in your company's currencyApproved automatically
A single purchase up to 1,000Group 1
Recurring fees up to 5,000 in total, for 12 months or lessGroup 1
Recurring fees up to 10,000 in total that can be ended without costGroup 1
Anything elseGroup 2
A renewal, by the value of one renewal termGoes toIts review opens
Up to 5,000, and it can be ended without costRenews without a decision3 months before the end
Up to 25,000, for 12 months or lessGroup 13 months before the end
Up to 100,000Group 29 months before the end
Anything elseGroup 212 months before the end

Your company may have changed them: the request form shows where yours will go before you submit. Nobody decides on their own request or on the renewal of a contract they own: they're left out of the group for that item.

4.4 A renewal review#

Each active contract with an end date gets one renewal review per term, opened by the daily job when the rule says. Approvers have until the notice deadline to decide.

At the end date, the daily job looks at the contract and its review:

The reviewThe contract renews automaticallyIt doesn't
Auto-approved, or ApprovedIt rolls over for its renewal termIt expires, unless the owner used Renew
PendingIt rolls over, and the review lapsesIt expires, and the review lapses
Not renewing, notice not recordedIt rolls over: "Renewed: notice not recorded"It's terminated
Notice sentIt's terminatedIt's terminated
No reviewIt rolls overIt expires

Rolling over moves the end date forward by the renewal term; the contract stays Active, and its next review opens in time for the next term.

A contract that doesn't renew by itself can still match an Auto-renew rule. That means no approval is needed, not that it renews: it ends at its end date unless its owner uses Renew. Home shows it as Renews automatically; the contract's own Renewal line says whether it does.

4.6 Working together#

  • Who sees what follows owners. Individuals see their own contracts and requests; Procurement Managers and Admins see everything. Approvers see in full what is sent to them, while it waits and afterwards.
  • Provider documents are kept by the Procurement Managers. Everyone else sees whether a provider is compliant.
  • Copy link on a record copies its address. Whoever opens it sees the record only if they may.
  • Two people, one record. If someone else saved the record while you were editing it, saving says "Someone else changed this record. Reload to see their changes." and your change isn't written. Reload, then make it again.
  • Owners: Procurement Managers change a contract's or a provider's owner. Whoever may change an obligation can give it to a colleague.

5. Finding things#

  • Search, at the top: part of a contract's title or counterparty, a provider's name or category, a purchase request's title, or an ID. It finds only what you can see.
  • List filters, and each list's own search box, as in chapter 2.
  • Export to Sheets on Contracts, Providers, Obligations, Purchases and Approvals makes a Google Sheet of what the list shows, with its filters. When it's ready, Open copy page opens Google's Make a copy page, which saves it in your own Drive.
  • Copy link on a record copies its address, for a colleague who can see it.

6. Reports#

Reports shows six reports on what you can see, each with a chart, a table and a sentence that sums it up. Choose Quarters back, Quarters ahead, Contract type, Provider and Approval group at the top. Procurement Managers and Admins also have Owner.

ReportAnswers
R-CP-1 Contracts to renew vs already renewed, by quarterHow many contracts came up for renewal each quarter: renewed (and how many automatically), ended, lapsed, and still to decide. The chart switches between Contracts and Renewal value
R-CP-2 Committed spend by quarterWhat approved purchase requests committed each quarter, single and recurring, and the yearly value of the active contracts
R-CP-3 ApprovalsDecisions each quarter: purchases approved, rejected and approved automatically, renewals approved, not renewed and lapsed; the median days to decide, and the rules used most
R-CP-4 Provider complianceProviders by compliance. Procurement Managers and Admins also see the documents expiring in the next 90 days
R-CP-5 Spend by providerThe top providers by committed value: their active contracts' yearly value plus the purchases approved this year, with their next renewal and compliance
S-05 Obligations performanceObligations due each quarter: done on time, done late, overdue and open, and the same by owner

Each report has Export to Sheets, Generate report (Doc) and Download PDF. At the top, Generate full report (Doc) and Download full PDF make one document with all six. When a Sheet or Doc is ready, Open copy page opens Google's Make a copy page, which saves it in your own Drive.

The scope line says what's counted: "Your records" for an Individual, "Whole organisation" for Procurement Managers and Admins. Quarters follow your company's financial year. Amounts aren't converted between currencies: committed spend and spend by provider count only your company's currency, and committed spend lists the others under its chart; renewal values add up every contract as it is.

7. For Procurement Managers#

Procurement Managers, and Admins, also:

  • see everything, with Mine and All on Home, All on Purchases, and the Owner filter on Contracts, Obligations and Reports;
  • add, change and archive provider documents, and see them on Home;
  • change a contract's or a provider's owner, and restore archived contracts and providers;
  • renew any contract and record its notice, and take the requester's steps on any purchase request, except editing a rejected one; they decide a request only when they're one of its approvers;
  • run Validate data and Import pasted rows, and change the rules and try them with Test a scenario, in Admin tools;
  • get the procurement overview email, daily or weekly, if your Admin set it: pending approvals, renewals due, notice deadlines, committed spend, compliance, the renewals and spend charts, and what needs a manager's attention.

8. Email and notifications#

  • If you ask for purchases, you get an email when your request is approved, approved automatically or rejected, with the approver's comment.
  • If you're an approver, you get "Approval needed" for each request and "Renewal decision needed" for each renewal sent to your group, with a link that opens it.
  • If you own contracts, you're emailed when a renewal decision needs you: to send notice, or to renew a contract that doesn't renew by itself.

The daily digest arrives around 07:00 on days when you have something: approvals waiting for you, what's happening to your contracts' renewals, notice deadlines and contracts ending, and obligations due. Every item links to the record. Your Admin turns it on or off for you.

Your settings (your initials, top right) holds your Theme: System, Light or Dark, kept on this device.

10. Using it on a phone#

Contracts & Providers works in your phone's browser; there's no app to install.

  • Every screen fits a phone. Lists become cards, and a record opens on its own, with ← Back to the list.
  • An approver can open the email's link, read the request with its value and rule, and approve it with a comment.
  • Open links from the app's emails in your browser, not inside the Gmail app.

11. When something goes wrong#

What you seeWhat it means
"Someone else changed this record. Reload to see their changes."Another person saved it first. Reload, then make your change again
"No approver is available for this request. Ask an admin to update the approval groups."You're the only approver in the group your request goes to. Ask your Admin
"A comment is required."Approving, rejecting and deciding a renewal need a comment
"The file is larger than 10 MB. Upload a smaller file, or paste a link instead."Upload a smaller file, or paste a link
"Possible duplicate" when you save a providerA provider with the same name or tax ID exists. Use it, or Save anyway if yours is a different one
"Google is busy right now. Please try again in a moment." or "The app is busy, please try again."Many changes at once. Try again
"That contract doesn't exist, or you can't see it."It's archived, or it isn't yours
"That item is no longer waiting for you."Another approver decided it, or it was cancelled
A request went to a group you didn't expectThe request shows which rule sent it. If the rule looks wrong, tell your Procurement Manager
You can't see a contract a colleague mentionsIndividuals see only their own. Ask its owner or a Procurement Manager
"Six7 Contracts & Providers is parked"The app is stopped for now, and nothing is lost. Ask the app's Admin when it will be back

Who to ask: your Procurement Manager, then the app's Admin.

A. Appendix: keyboard#

Everything works from the keyboard: Tab moves between controls, Enter opens or presses them, and Esc closes a dialog or clears the search.

B. Appendix: words used in the app#

WordMeaning
ContractAn agreement with a provider, customer, landlord or partner, with its dates, value and exit terms
CounterpartyWho a contract is with
ProviderA company you buy from
ComplianceWhether a provider's documents are in date: OK, Expiring, Expired or No documents
Purchase requestA request to buy something, with a number such as PR-0012
Single purchaseA one-off purchase, with one price
Recurring feesA service paid every month, quarter or year, for a committed term
TCVTotal contract value: the price, or the setup fee plus every payment of the term
Renewal TCVThe value of one renewal term of a contract
If we end it earlyWhat ending a contract early costs: nothing, an early-termination fee, or the rest of the term
Notice periodHow many days before the end date the counterparty must be told the contract won't renew
Notice deadlineThe last day to give that notice: the end date minus the notice period
Renews automaticallyThe contract continues for another term unless notice is given
Renewal reviewThe decision on whether a contract renews, due by its notice deadline
LapsedA renewal review nobody decided before the end date
Group 1, Group 2Your company's standard and senior approvers
RuleOne line of your company's approval policy, such as P3 or R2
ObligationSomething a contract commits you to do by a date
ExpiringA contract ending in the next 90 days, or a document expiring in the next 30
Notice dueA notice deadline in the next 30 days, or one that has passed while the contract still runs
FY2026 Q4A quarter of your financial year, named by the year it ends in
DigestThe daily email with what needs you
